How does that work out for you? As a developer, I've noticed a big change recently in which websites are relying more and more on javascript. A lot of websites just plain won't function anymore without it, with the rise of client-side templating such as angularJS.

As someone who blocks javascript by default, I usually end up allowing select scripts. The issue is that allowing Recaptcha allows a lot of google's scripts. Voat works pretty nicely without most javascript.
It kind of freaks me out realizing how much crap you have to let through for certain websites to work. I would agree that voat is pretty okay when it comes to browsing without JS though.

It is a pain in the ass. I use noscript, which allows me to temporarily enable it for certain websites and such, so often if a site doesn't work with javascript I will temporarily pop it on. The other thing I do is use mobile sites. Facebook, for example; (when I log in once a month of so) has a fairly easy to use mobile site, even in a desktop web browser.

Basically it sucks and I wish more devs would try not to use javascript unless they really have to. It isn't like that is going to happen though.

There are a ton of legitimate reasons to encourage javascript usage. It's very unefficient to send a whole website repeatedly when a user just needs a small part updated. I wish that javascript had some sort of permissions system (sort of like apps on android) so that you could feel safe using javascript, instead of being tracked/other malicious things.

I understand why JS is used and it makes sense for most people. For people who don't care about the security issues (most users) it is fantastic, so why wouldn't you develop with it? I mean who doesn't want what javascript has to offer right? If there was a permission system I would be happy to start using it.

Ok /v/smashbros, my question twofold: Which character do you main and what's one tip for playing as and one tip for playing against that character?

I'm a bowser main in smash 4,

My tip for playing as him: Dtilt is actually one of your best kill moves, try hitting someone with it near the ledge.

My tip for playing against him: get him in the air. Like any other turtle, he's weak when you're underneath him. Just wait out his Dair and DownB, then punish.

Falco in melee and Project M.

At my (rusty) level, I'd say the most useful tool is clever use of dair over any shine fanciness or laser spamming. Dair has excellent priority and hit-stuns both fast fallers and slow fallers.

Playing against Falco: force him to the ledge with whatever you got. Being able to accomplish this differs, depending on what you're playing and the Falco's tendencies. But generally a powershielded laser and a throw towards the closest ledge does it. Then reads and punishes are generally easy; ledge hop double laser = shield-grab or any aerial OOS and ledge hop forward-B = shield, roll and punish.

gotta be careful of where you start the dair, if you start it too low on their shield it's an incredibly easy punish. shine "fanciness" is very useful; pillaring and shine-bairs are the most prominent examples - and if you watch any tournaments, westballz makes falco multishines a terrifyingly fast way to make his opponent's shields disappear. uptilt also sets up for a crap ton of stuff

near the ledge is where falco is the most deadly, normally, so i assume from this you are having trouble playing with your back to the ledge. that's something i can talk about in the matchup thread if you have anything specific you want to talk about on that
also DOUBLE LASER FROM THE LEDGE IS NOT SAFE

Yeah, I've started to force myself to stop double lasering from ledge. It's extremely situational. I actually do have some trouble facing my back towards the ledge while near it, but I've started to find ways to regain stage presence. Actually, rolling isn't as bad as I've taught my instincts, especially when coupled with a ledge dash.

Regarding shine fanciness - I view westballz as the best Falco player currently,. It's amazing what he's been able to accomplish with the character, but he's still only showing (growing) potential. I'd say that PPMD is still the most consistent Falco (once he brings it out), and the shine fanciness I see from him is at most a shine grab here and there.

falco's roll isn't awful, but it definitely isn't something you are going to want to be doing often by any stretch of the word, especially considering how hard falco can get punished. try shinestalling when you are recovering high; practice side-b shortening mixups, and ESPECIALLY practice walljumping into side-b/up-b sweetspot/jump back on the ledge or directly onto the stage. walljump into dair is super swag.

one of the biggest strengths of falco, and a huge part of his glass-cannon identity, is his ability to extend combos FOREVER. westballz is by far the best at that right now, and given his very fast fingers can abuse shine's power a lot more and capitalize on very quick setups or multishine.

given that we haven't seen ppmd's falco in many many months, i can't say whether he is consistent, but i will say that a lot of his gameplan doesn't as much revolve around constant pressure and defense through trades and persistent offense(how westballz plays), which is a big part of why shine doesn't come out as often. he certainly does more stuff with it than shinegrab though, shine bair/uptilt setups etc are way too good to pass up on nowadays.

Yes, there's a very good point to the mindset that goes into mango's style of teching: flick the stick; if you don't know where you're going, the opponent doesn't either. Same goes for mixing up recovery to and from the ledge.

The best I can say to back up my statement regarding PPDM is that comparing his play (rarely as we see it) to westballz's, it's a lot less button-y and pressurizing, while perhaps more calculated and controlling. It goes further than just shine grabs though :)

Smash 4: Captain Falcon

As: Your game should be all about punishing. Your approach options are very limited and easily countered. Try to make your opponent nervous as opposed to actually hitting them by doing things like bair approaches and wait for them to make a mistake. Killing your opponent off stage is your greatest strength. Mix up walk off dairs, bairs, and uairs to keep your opponent guessing. Another mix up is to predict the air dodge, walk off, let them dodge and immediately jump -> dair to punish.

Against: Pick anyone with a good projectile. It's so hard to get in and fight which Captain Falcon needs to do. Hardest MUs are Sheik, Pikachu, and Villager.

PM: Mario

As: Mario has four great options to gimp opponents off stage. For people who have easy to predict recoveries (CF, Ganon, Spacies, etc) wait for them recovery and cape them. Your cape reaches below the ledge as well so it's possible to cape low recoveries without endangering yourself by going off stage. If you notice a pattern in your opponents recovery, space out a fair and go for the meteor! Even if you do not space it properly, you still Dr. Mario's fair power and can kill them off the side anyway. Mario's bair and nair both have good knock back and are safer options to the fair (though not as powerful)

Against: Mario's greatest weakness is his range. His longest ranged move (fsmash) is out ranged by all FE characters and CF/Ganon. He also has quite a bit of ending lag on all of his specials so wait for one of them and punish.

It's not really that "Unity C#" uses the "Start()" method, rather the "MonoBehaviour" class certainly does. I assume in the backend (correct me if I'm wrong) they could use a form of "Main()" function.

I'm probably a bit naive, but isn't Main() meant to ever only run once and there can ever be only one Main() throughout a program? By utilizing Start() you can still get the run once per instance of the script, while allowing more than one Start() throughout the entire program. Of course this is purely guess work.
